module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Imaginary part of $\prod_{k=0}^n (1 + k \cdot i)$, $i = \sqrt{-1}$

*References:*
- [A105751](https://oeis.org/A105751)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Complex Filter Topology Nat

namespace OeisA105751

/--
The primary defining sequence `a`.
a n is the imaginary part of $\prod_{k=0}^n (1 + k \cdot i)$, where $i = \sqrt{-1}$.
-/
noncomputable def a (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  let productTerm (k : ℕ) : ℂ := 1 + (k : ℂ) * I
  Int.floor (((Finset.range (n + 1)).prod productTerm).im)

/-- Term theorems verifying the first few values of the sequence against the official OEIS b-file -/
@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 0 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 1 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 3 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 0 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = -40 := by
  delta a; norm_num [Finset.prod]

/--
Numerical calculation suggests that a similar division holds in this case.
Type 1: primes p that do not divide any element of the sequence {$a(n)$}.
In this case, unlike in A105750, the set of type 1 primes is empty;
that is, every prime p divides some term of this sequence.

Note: The triangular number n*(n+1)/2 divides $a(n)$ (see A164652).
In particular, if $p$ is an odd prime then $p$ divides $a(p)$. For $p=2$, $2$ divides $a(4)=-40$.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem prime_divides_some_term (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ∣ a n := by
  sorry

/--
Moll's conjecture 5.5 extends to this sequence and takes the form:
(i) the $2$-adic valuation $\nu_2(a(n)) \sim n/4$ as n -> oo.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using formal_conjectures at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a105751-two-adic/blob/a9692d90078c4dff1478acaaa70be2fba06a3ef9/lean/OeisA105751TwoAdicFC.lean#L980-L985"]
theorem conjecture :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ (4 : ℚ) * (padicValInt 2 (a n) : ℚ) / (n : ℚ)) atTop (nhds 1) := by
  sorry

/--
Moll's conjecture 5.5 extends to this sequence and takes the form:
(ii) for the other primes of type $2$, the p-adic valuation
$\nu_p(a(n)) \sim n/(p - 1)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$.

(Type 2 primes consists of primes p == 1 (mod 4))
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem conjecture.variants.moll_p_mod_4_eq_1 {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) (h_mod : p % 4 = 1) :
    Tendsto (fun n ↦ ((p - 1 : ℚ) * (padicValInt p (a n) : ℚ)) / (n : ℚ)) atTop (nhds 1) := by
  sorry

end OeisA105751

findings.description: The statement `∀ p, p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ∣ a n` is trivially true because the sequence has zero terms: `a 0 = 0` and `a 3 = 0`, both proved in the file as `a_0` and `a_3`, and every integer divides 0. I compiled `example (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : ∃ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ∣ a n := ⟨0, by rw [a_0]; exact dvd_zero _⟩` against the file. Primality is not even needed: `example (p : ℤ) : ∃ n : ℕ, p ∣ a n := ⟨3, by rw [a_3]; exact dvd_zero _⟩` also compiles. So the declaration says nothing about divisibility of the sequence. The source's claim is non-trivial: every prime divides some genuine (non-zero) term, so no prime is of Moll's Type 1. The docstring itself argues this way. It gives the non-zero witness a(4) = -40 for p = 2 and 'p divides a(p)' for odd p, rather than a(0) = 0. That suggests the trivial witness was not noticed. Restricting to `0 < n` would not repair it, because `a 3 = 0`.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS A105751 (read via the oeisdata mirror of the entry, revision #34, Feb 22 2024), comment by Peter Bala, Jun 01 2023: "Moll (2012) studied the prime divisors of the terms of A105750 and divided the primes into three classes. Numerical calculation suggests that a similar division holds in this case. Type 1: primes p that do not divide any element of the sequence {a(n)}. In this case, unlike in A105750, the set of type 1 primes is empty; that is, every prime p divides some term of this sequence." Formula section (Bala, May 27 2023): "The triangular number n*(n+1)/2 divides a(n). See A164652. In particular, if p is an odd prime then p divides a(p)." Data: a(0)=0, a(3)=0 (b-file). The classification comes from V. H. Moll, 'An arithmetic conjecture on a sequence of arctangent sums' (2012). Note 5.4 there reads: "Type 1. The prime p does not divide any element of the sequence f_n. The first few examples are {3, 7, 11, 23, 31, 47, 59}", and the introduction says "primes p which never divide an element of the sequence f_n". Here f_n = ±Re ∏(1+ik), which has no zero terms, so in Moll's setting Type 1 is a meaningful, non-trivial notion. For A105751 it becomes trivial only because of the zero terms.
findings.suggested_fix: theorem prime_divides_some_term (p : ℕ) (hp : p.Prime) : ∃ n : ℕ, a n ≠ 0 ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ a n. For prime p this is equivalent to `∃ n, 0 < padicValInt p (a n)`, which matches Moll's valuation-based classification. I checked the corrected form computationally for all primes p < 120 using non-zero witnesses (p=2: n=4; p=3: n=2; p=5: n=4; ...). I also checked that p ∣ a(p) with a(p) ≠ 0 for every odd prime 5 ≤ p < 150. So it is true and non-trivial, and remains textbook-level: it follows from n(n+1)/2 ∣ a(n) together with non-vanishing.

reformulations.difference: The source's asymptotic equivalence ν₂(a(n)) ~ n/4 is stated as `Tendsto (fun n ↦ 4 * padicValInt 2 (a n) / n) atTop (nhds 1)` in ℚ. The function takes junk values at n = 0 (x/0 = 0) and at the zero terms a 0 = a 3 = 0 (padicValInt 2 0 = 0).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: f ~ g with g(n) = n/4 ≠ 0 for n ≥ 1 means f(n)/g(n) → 1, which is 4f(n)/n → 1. The junk values occur at finitely many n (a(n) = 0 only at n = 0, 3; checked up to n = 200), so they do not affect the limit. Convergence in ℚ of a ℚ-valued sequence to a rational limit is the same as convergence in ℝ, since ℚ carries the subspace topology. The external formal proof makes this transfer explicitly with `Rat.isEmbedding_coe_real.tendsto_nhds_iff`.

sources_consulted: https://oeis.org/A105751 (main page blocked by Cloudflare; entry text read from the OEIS data mirror https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A105/A105751.seq, revision #34, Feb 22 2024)
V. H. Moll, An arithmetic conjecture on a sequence of arctangent sums (2012), https://www.tulane.edu/~vhm/papers_html/xn-final.pdf (Introduction, Theorem 2.4, Note 5.4, Conjecture 5.5)

https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-a105751-two-adic/blob/a9692d90078c4dff1478acaaa70be2fba06a3ef9/lean/OeisA105751TwoAdicFC.lean (fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com and compiled locally against this commit)
review.notes:
1) Definition `a`: I proved in Lean that `a n = (∏ k ∈ range (n+1), (⟨1,k⟩ : GaussianInt)).im` for all n, using only standard axioms. So the `Int.floor` encoding is exact. A computable version matches the b-file for n = 0..20 and the 5-adic valuations in the OEIS example.

2) `conjecture` (research solved): I compiled the linked external file (`A105751Proof.oeisA105751_conjecture`, lines 980–985) against this exact commit. There were no errors or warnings, and `#print axioms` gives [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. A `rfl` check confirms that its type is identical to `OeisA105751.conjecture`. The proof establishes exact formulas: ν₂(a(4m+1)) = ν₂(a(4m+2)) = m, ν₂(a(4m)) = m+2+ν₂(⌈m/2⌉) and ν₂(a(4m+3)) = m+3+ν₂(⌈m/2⌉). The 'solved' status is therefore correct, although the OEIS entry still calls it a conjecture. Metadata nit, not mathematics: the attribute uses kind `formal_conjectures` ('formally proved in this repository'), but the proof lives in a separate, non-fork repository. By FormalConjecturesUtil/Attributes/Basic.lean the kind should be `lean4`, as other files do for the same author's external repositories (e.g. GraphConjecture316).

3) `conjecture.variants.moll_p_mod_4_eq_1` (research open): the source's (ii) is stated for 'the other primes of type 2'. The Lean uses the hypothesis p ≡ 1 (mod 4), which the same OEIS comment conjectures to be exactly the odd type-2 primes. I consider this a faithful modelling choice, not a defect. Primes p ≡ 3 (mod 4) can never be type 2. Such p are inert in ℤ[i], so P_n = ∏(1+ki) is a unit mod p. If p^k divides both a(n) and a(n+1), then p^k ∣ n+1, so the valuation cannot grow linearly. The Lean therefore loses nothing from (ii) and only adds the source's own conjecture that every p ≡ 1 (mod 4) is type 2. The encoding (p−1)·ν_p(a(n))/n → 1 is correct, and the zero terms and n = 0 affect finitely many n only. I know of no resolution of (ii); the OEIS entry is unchanged since Feb 2024 as of the mirror, which includes revisions up to May 2026. I could not run a broader literature search (no search tool, GitHub rate-limited).

4) The five test values a 0..a 4 = 0, 1, 3, 0, −40 match the b-file.

demonstrated.claim: The statement exactly as the file gives it (`type_of% @OeisA105751.prime_divides_some_term`) is proved in one line with witness n = 0, because `a 0 = 0` (the file's own `a_0`) and every integer divides 0; primality is never used, so the declaration says nothing about the source's claim that every prime divides a non-zero term. A second example shows that restricting to `0 < n` would still be trivial, via `a 3 = 0` (the file's `a_3`).

submission.summary: `/workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean` imports `FormalConjectures.OEIS.«105751»` and proves `OeisA105751.prime_divides_some_term` exactly as stated, in one term-mode line: `fun _p _hp => ⟨0, by rw [OeisA105751.a_0]; exact dvd_zero _⟩`. It works because the sequence has a zero term, `a 0 = 0`. A second `example` shows that adding `0 < n` would still be trivial, because `a 3 = 0` is also a zero term. So the fix has to require `a n ≠ 0`. The file compiles with no errors, no warnings and no `sorry`. `#print axioms` on the main theorem reports only `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, which also confirms that the file's own `a_0` is fully proved.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.OEIS.«105751»

/-!
`OeisA105751.prime_divides_some_term` is meant to say that every prime divides some genuine
(non-zero) term of A105751, so that no prime is of Moll's "Type 1". As formalized it is
trivially true: the sequence has zero terms, `a 0 = 0` and `a 3 = 0` (the file's own `a_0`,
`a_3`), and every integer divides `0`.
-/

-- OeisA105751.prime_divides_some_term
--   (∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ∣ a n):
-- provable in one line with the degenerate witness `n = 0`, because `a 0 = 0` (the file's
-- `a_0`); the primality hypothesis is never used.
theorem prime_divides_some_term_trivial : type_of% @OeisA105751.prime_divides_some_term :=
  fun _p _hp => ⟨0, by rw [OeisA105751.a_0]; exact dvd_zero _⟩

-- Requiring `0 < n` would not repair it: `a 3 = 0` (the file's `a_3`) is another zero term.
example (p : ℕ) : ∃ n : ℕ, 0 < n ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ OeisA105751.a n :=
  ⟨3, by norm_num, by rw [OeisA105751.a_3]; exact dvd_zero _⟩

#print axioms prime_divides_some_term_trivial

submission.summary:
Fixed `OeisA105751.prime_divides_some_term`. The old statement `∃ n : ℕ, (p : ℤ) ∣ a n` could be proved in one line with the witness `a 0 = 0`. It is now `∃ n : ℕ, a n ≠ 0 ∧ (p : ℤ) ∣ a n`, which says what the source means: every prime divides a non-zero term, so no prime is of Moll's Type 1. Adding only `0 < n` would not have been enough, because `a 3 = 0` as well.

I added one sentence to the docstring: "The terms $a(0) = a(3) = 0$ are divisible by every prime, so we ask for a nonzero term $a(n)$; otherwise the statement would be trivially true." The rest of the docstring, the `@[category textbook, AMS 11]` attribute and every other declaration are unchanged. `textbook` still fits, because the corrected claim follows from n(n+1)/2 ∣ a(n) and a(n) being non-zero.

Checks:
- With `lake env lean --json` the file reports only the three `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings it had before.
- With the `FormalConjectures` library's lakefile options passed as `-D` flags (`warn.sorry=false`, the category, AMS and LaTeX-docstring linters), it reports nothing. Deleting the `category` attribute in a scratch copy made those linters complain, so they were really running.
- In a scratch file, the witnesses n = 0 and n = 3 no longer satisfy the new statement. Non-zero witnesses do (p = 2 with a 4 = -40, p = 3 with a 2 = 3). Earlier I checked the corrected claim for every prime below 120.

The only diff is this file. The modified `lakefile.toml` and the untracked `run/` in `git status` were already there before my session (timestamped 12:21). I did not touch them.
